# OntoSmith

> An ontology-driven knowledge-graph builder: design the ontology first (schema, definitions, boundary examples — approved by a human, shipped as a versioned, hash-pinned pack), then build the graph under it with a pipeline that separates proposing from judging. Models propose candidates; deterministic gates and a fitted decision model (Jev, a pinned component) decide what is written. Every triple carries its evidence span and provenance; every operating point is adopted through a pre-registered measurement gate. The built graph serves through hybrid retrieval (vector + lexical + graph), a sample API, and a minimal demo app. MIT-licensed; the quality record — scores with scope, method, and failure anatomy, failures included — is published in the project whitepaper and is reproducible from the shipped adjudication appendix.
>
> Scope, stated plainly: the schema is a flat extraction contract — a closed inventory of entity and relation types with definitions and boundary examples, drafted or imported, approved by a human, judged per type by the decision model. It is not a formal ontology: no class hierarchy, no inheritance, no logical axioms — OntoSmith is not an OWL ontology editor and runs no inference over the graph. The flatness is deliberate (per-type decisions are what make quality measurable); the job is turning a document corpus into a governed, evidence-carrying graph for search and agents.

## Product

- [README](README.md): what OntoSmith is, the no-key first steps, the six-step loop, the packs, and the command map
- [Whitepaper](docs/whitepaper.md): the long-form technical report and the canonical quality record (§5) — system, method, measured scores with intervals, failure anatomy, gate adoptions and rejections, cost accounting, limitations
- [Connections](docs/connections.md): the connection layer — seats, the reference profile (default preset), recommended models, the custom-binding contract, and `ontosmith configure`, the wizard (with its template twin) that declares bindings
- [Serving](docs/serving.md): the one graph in Neo4j, `ontosmith search`, the sample API, and the demo app
- [Hands-on guide](docs/hands-on.md): the whole loop in three tracks over your own documents — the quickstart build, the same build under an ontology domain pack, and drafting your own pack with the ontology builder — plus an appendix track
- [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md): every `ontosmith` command and its options, refreshed by hand from the live `--help` surface — the file says so in its own header
- [Pack design](docs/PACK_DESIGN.md): the pack-format contract — what a pack is, its files, and the rules it is loaded, versioned, and measured under
- [Adjudication contract](docs/ADJUDICATION.md): the standing specification for machine adjudication in the quality records, including the six seam rulings

## Quality records and evidence

- [Benchmarks index](benchmarks/README.md): the claim-level index — every published number with its scope, the harness that produces it, and its readout
- [Re-DocRED record (pointer)](benchmarks/redocred.md): the flagship build's scope, replay path, and the failure-anatomy data block the chart renderer parses
- [BioRED & CUAD records (pointer)](benchmarks/biored-cuad.md): the supporting records' scope and where their data lives (pack conformance entries CR-1…CR-7, CC-1…CC-4)
- [Adjudication appendix](benchmarks/appendix/README.md): the flagship record's samples, key files, and verdicts — machine judgments, labeled as such — plus the raw census scores; a replay recomputes every headline from these files alone
- [Reproduce](reproduce/README.md): every headline figure mapped to the command that recomputes it — or marked as record data when a figure is not reader-recomputable

## Examples

- [Examples index](examples/README.md): the walkthrough map — recorded reference artefact, demo corpus, and the replay/fetch demo tooling
